title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
focus: superstition used against a credulous man

teacherSummary.text: In the Dutch hamlet of Sleepy Hollow, lanky, superstitious schoolmaster Ichabod Crane courts the heiress Katrina Van Tassel, partly for her father's rich farm. His rival is the strong prankster Brom Bones. After a party where ghost stories are told, Ichabod rides home and is chased by a Headless Horseman who hurls his head at him. Ichabod disappears; a shattered pumpkin is found. Brom marries Katrina and looks knowing when the tale is told.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “The Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow” slowly and put it in my own words: The narrator names the valley's chief ghost: the Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow. Next, craft. I notice the repeated "H" sounds, which make the name easy to repeat like a local legend. The strongest word is “Headless”: the missing head is the frightening detail people remember. Then, effect. How does the name of the ghost work on the reader and the townspeople? My answer: The name already makes the ghost a legend that everyone in the valley tells; that shared story is what Brom later uses to frighten Ichabod away.
